title: Remote ticfac/run-* branches of runs that ended accumulate on origin: retire them by rule
description:
Measured 2026-09-30: origin holds 281 heads, 205 of them ticfac/run-<run id>/... job branches from 14 runs (9 local epic-<id> runs, 5 cloud run_<hex> runs). 71 belong to epics already closed (gvc 15, 9pd 27, xte 19, wne 10); epic-2jn alone holds 69. Nothing deletes them: the leftover sweep (internal/reconcile/sweep.go) removes a job's LOCAL branch and, since tyv, the closed tick's wip refs on the remote, but never the job branch on origin. The whole-repo branch listing tick hn6's cloud run broke on (fixed separately by scoping the listing to the run's own prefixes) was one symptom; the growth itself remains.

Proposed rule (not executed; nothing has been deleted):
1. Retire only branches under ticfac/run-<run id>/ whose run has ENDED and will not be resumed under that id: the epic is closed, or a later run id has started for the same epic (a stopped run may be resumed by id and adopts its attempts by branch identity, so a merely stopped run's branches stay).
2. A branch whose head is contained in the epic branch or the base branch (merged), or that carries no commit beyond the base it was cut from, is deleted at that point: it holds nothing the history does not.
3. A branch holding commits nothing merged (a rejected attempt) is KEPT, as disposal keeps it, until the epic has been closed for 14 days; the run feed names its head sha. Then it is deleted.
4. The rule runs where the sweep already runs (run end, and run start for closed ticks/epics), and as a factory-side pass for cloud runs whose container is gone; a failed delete is recorded and left for the next pass, never a refusal of the run.
5. Delete by exact ref name computed from the run id, never by a pattern wider than one run's namespace, and never touch epic/, tick-run/ or tick/ branches or anything a person owns (branch-ownership registry).

Done when: a test proves a run's merged/empty job branches are gone from a fake origin after its epic closes, an unmerged one survives until the grace expires, a stopped-but-resumable run keeps all of its branches, and the next cleanup on this repository leaves origin with no ticfac/run-* branch of a closed epic older than the grace.
